title: Chapter 34: Goodwill
html:
Chen Ge sat alone in the dark with four rag dolls arranged before him. Without context, the scene would have looked ridiculous—or deeply unsettling.

“I don’t know exactly how you ended up in my Haunted House, and I’m not sure what to call you, but I can promise one thing: I’m not here to hurt you.”

His voice echoed softly. He wanted some response badly enough to prove his theory, yet part of him was relieved when the dolls remained still.

After several seconds, he tried another approach. “Murder by Midnight was created from what happened at Fu An Apartments. If I’m right, the four of you represent the family who died there.”

The room seemed to grow colder. The door clicked shut behind him, and nearby furniture trembled faintly.

“But the case has finally been solved. The person responsible has been caught, and the police are handling the rest.” Trying not to sound nervous, Chen Ge pulled up the morning news on his phone. “Look. It’s right here—and I helped them find him.”

Chen Ge knew the dolls’ lingering resentment was tied to Wang Qi, so he hoped proof of the arrest would calm them. It did not work as well as he had expected.

The atmosphere remained cold and tense. The greatest problem was obvious: he had no reliable way to communicate with whatever was attached to the dolls. Still, he refused to give up. The Haunted House was everything he had; leaving four unpredictable supernatural presences completely unmanaged was not an option.

“I’m trying to help you.” The dolls offered no visible response.

“Then I only have one thing left to try.” Chen Ge took out Wang Qi’s yellowed missing-person notice. The moment it appeared, the restless movement in the room eased and the pressure in the air seemed to lessen.

“This is what you wanted?” He placed the notice among the four dolls. As soon as they touched it, the paper began fluttering violently despite the still air.

There was no draft, yet both the notice and the dolls trembled. A vague image seemed to surface on the paper for an instant, resembling Wang Qi’s face. Before Chen Ge could examine it, the notice tore into pieces that vanished among the four dolls. Then the room became quiet again.

“That’s it?”

The black phone vibrated. Another notification had appeared.

“Hidden Mission complete: Murder by Midnight. Specter Affinity +1. You have earned the goodwill of the lingering spirits of Ping An Apartments. They will help maintain the Murder by Midnight scenario each day.”

Chen Ge stared at the message for a long moment. “So that was the scenario’s only Hidden Mission?”

He mentally organized everything he had learned.A Trial Mission completion rate above ninety percent unlocks a Hidden Item, and that Hidden Item can be the key to the scenario’s Hidden Mission. If I want full control over future scenarios, I should aim for more than ninety percent completion whenever possible.

Looking back, simply staying inside Ping An Apartments until dawn would probably have completed the Trial Mission, but it would not have earned him the missing-person notice.

That system is devious. It rewards the player for investigating every strange detail instead of taking the safest route.He searched the black phone for more information. The first page he checked was My Team of Ghosts and Ghouls, but to his disappointment, the list was still empty.

The message says I gained the goodwill of the lingering spirits, but they aren’t listed here. Maybe they haven’t formally joined me—or perhaps “lingering spirits” are a different category from ghosts and ghouls.

There was no explanation. He opened My Item Storage instead and found that Wang Qi’s Missing-Person Notice was still listed, but its Malice Points had fallen to zero.

So what exactly were the Malice Points measuring? And why did resolving the spirits’ grievance consume them?

A hidden system was gradually revealing itself. Chen Ge had no idea which details would matter later, so he committed all of them to memory before standing up.I still can’t communicate with them directly, but they’re willing to help maintain the scenario. Overall, that is definitely a win.

Keeping a large scenario clean and functional took time and money. If the lingering spirits truly handled some of that work, they would save him considerable effort. Looking at the four dolls, Chen Ge found that most of his earlier fear had faded.Maybe hiring ghosts for the Haunted House isn’t such a ridiculous idea after all.

At the doorway, he glanced back. The dolls representing the parents and older sister remained where he had placed them, but the smallest doll had tipped onto its side again, suspiciously close to the edge of the group as though preparing another escape.

Chen Ge sighed. Not every supernatural presence seemed cruel or hostile. The smallest doll, at least, reminded him more of a curious kitten—eager to explore, but easily frightened.

“Little one, stop wandering around. Someone might step on you.”

He left the room with a better understanding of what the black phone’s scenarios might actually represent.Maybe these scenarios aren’t only meant to frighten visitors. Each one has a story, a reason it exists, and something left unresolved. Unlocking them might also be giving these displaced spirits somewhere to belong.

Chen Ge switched off his flashlight and walked alone through the dark corridor. Once he was sure no visitor—or ghost—could hear him, a sly grin spread across his face. “They’re naturally good at frightening people, they don’t need salaries, and they apparently help with maintenance. They might be the perfect employees.”

The thought of his Haunted House’s future restored his energy immediately.

“This test has gone on long enough. Three visitors are still inside. Now, who do I find first?”
